title: FIFA World Cup 2026
client: Motorola Mobility, a Lenovo Company; FIFA World Cup 26™
onePhraser: The World Cup doesn’t just change what you watch. It changes how you dress, move, and show up.
longDescription: For one month, a shirt becomes a flag. Face paint becomes pride. Hair becomes a declaration. The street, the rooftop, the alley behind the bar, matter as much as what happens in the stadium - that's where the real self-expression happens. And it happens through a phone in someone's hand.  That's the territory we found for Motorola's FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign. Motorola has been building a design-forward identity for years — color partnerships with Pantone, craft with Swarovski, sound with Bose. Each one making the case that a phone isn't just a device, it's an expressive object. FIFA is where that argument goes global. Five billion viewers. 211 nations. All of them holding a phone, wanting to capture something. "Football is Calling" doesn't sell camera specs or battery life. It sells the idea that your Football Self — the one who breaks every routine, befriends every rival, climbs every rooftop — deserves a phone that matches who you become when the Cup arrives.  Lifestyle Tech isn't a product category. It's a positioning. And the World Cup is the biggest stage on earth to prove it.
notes: Reference example. Replace draft copy and add final Google Drive links before approval.

title: Wandinha S02 — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Contextualized OOH stunts in Wednesday's acidic voice
longDescription: The Wednesday Season 2 Brazil launch campaign built cultural conversation through bold, site-specific stunts rather than a conventional media push: contextualized OOH carrying "acidic phrases" written in Wednesday's voice, placed at culturally relevant locations across Brazilian cities. The centerpiece was a mural on the Minhocão viaduct in São Paulo by artist Aline Bispo, which generated major organic conversation despite triggering controversy and a fine under the city's clean-city law. When an original activation planned for Pelourinho in Salvador was cancelled and singer Ana Castela declined a planned talent tie-in late in the process, the team pivoted to a new activation, "Estação das Sombras," and an AV transformation featuring Boca Rosa. The retrospective credits the team's resilience through repeated direction changes, while flagging that neither the late talent decline nor the OOH fine had a pre-mapped contingency plan. The campaign is flagged internally as case-study-ready and awards-worthy.

title: One Piece S02 — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Chico Bento x One Piece crossover launch campaign
longDescription: The One Piece S02 launch campaign for Netflix Brazil hinged on a single crossover idea: pairing the straw hat of Luffy with Chico Bento, the iconic Mauricio de Sousa Productions (MSP) character, treating both hats as a shared symbol bridging anime and Brazilian pop culture. What started as a small insight grew into a fully integrated rollout: a hero film ("Jornada dos Sonhos") where 2D Chico Bento falls into the Going Merry world and is swallowed by Laboon before waking with Luffy's hat; a video call between Iñaki Godoy and Chico about trading hats; wanted-poster exchanges between Netflix and MSP's social accounts; an Eiichiro Oda talent video; a Laboon activation on Copacabana beach; a Gabriel Medina collaboration; and bespoke stretched-Luffy OOH. It launched March 9, 2026 and passed 85 million views across assets, with the hero film drawing 46.9 million views and the Iñaki call earning the highest engagement rate (4.09%). The retrospective noted the two-straw-hats connection could have been explored further, and that MSP's production pace strained against ad deadlines (17 edit versions in two days).

title: Sintonia S05 — Campaign + Event
onePhraser: Series finale campaign built around a live fan event
longDescription: Sintonia S05 closed out one of Brazil's biggest series with an integrated campaign and a festival-scale live event, "O Último Baile," built to celebrate the franchise across five seasons and formally say goodbye to it. The creative approach used 3D identity visual elements and cast the character Pulga as the protagonist of event communications, carrying through into a bold, motion-based "Abraço" key art that Netflix backed despite the risk, plus AV recap explorations. The tagline "O Último Corre," established during the Season 4 process, carried through to the finale. Deliverables spanned identity toolkit, social title assets, bespoke media, and real-time event coverage. Season 4 reference assets performed strongly (a main vertical key art hit 70% engagement rate), and the retrospective noted the project delivered a five-month production for an event that typically needs a full year, with several strong creative ideas cut along the way.

title: Griselda — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: A weeping Narcos crossover film: Pablo Triste
longDescription: Launch campaign for Griselda, Netflix's Sofia Vergara series on cocaine trafficker Griselda Blanco, adapted for the Brazilian market. Creative development centered on a character-driven film called "Pablo Triste" and a concept tying the show into the Narcos universe, alongside a "Ficha Criminal" (criminal record) idea. Original music was researched (Hefty) and composed (Pingado) specifically for the campaign. The Pablo Triste AV reached 14.9M views and 47,459 engagements (0.32% engagement rate). Retrospective learnings flagged friction in OOH vendor management and coordination issues with production house The End.

title: Alice in Borderland S3 — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Drone spectacle and prayer-chain stunt for the finale
longDescription: Launch campaign for the final season of Alice in Borderland, built to beat S1/S2 conversation volume and ride the momentum of Squid Game S3. Three ideas were approved straight out of Round 1: a drone show over Curitiba, chosen specifically for production feasibility and visual novelty; "Arisu Vivera," a collaboration with the popular account Padre Patrick that leaned into real fandom behavior by staging prayer-chain-style engagement; and Tudum Charts, an interactive platform pitched as a potential permanent Netflix global asset. The drone video hit 10M views on TikTok, becoming one of the most-viewed pieces ever on Netflix Brasil's profile, with unplanned amplification from Curitiba's city government and local press. Not everything landed: Tudum Charts never got a structured rollout, and Padre posted about a Netflix competitor after signing an exclusivity agreement.

title: Caramelo — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Swapping film stars for shelter dogs up for adoption
longDescription: Launch campaign for the Netflix film Caramelo, run against a hard KPI set from the outset: drive real dog adoptions. The unifying idea, "Protagonistas," put actual shelter dogs in the place of movie posters — professional portrait-style key art of adoptable dogs, an ASMR video with the film's canine cast, a music video for an original IZA track, and a nationwide adoption platform built with Instituto Caramelo, including a dedicated site with real dog profiles and a trending-audio social collab with Iza. Results: 12 real dogs adopted (including a 10-year-old named Bernadete and a three-legged dog nicknamed Caramelo da Upa), a 132% jump in adoption-related searches in week one, 133K+ unique site visits and 180 adoption forms submitted, an ASMR video that passed 15M views, and Caramelo becoming the most-watched Brazilian film in Netflix history, reaching the Top 10 in 90 countries. One approved idea, a platform concept called "Augoritmos," had to be dropped after technical limitations surfaced too late to build a substitute.

title: Um Tira da Pesada 4 — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Eddie Murphy's Brazilian doubles for Beverly Hills Cop 4
longDescription: For the Brazilian launch of Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F (Um Tira da Pesada 4), the campaign built on the franchise's deep local nostalgia — the film was long a staple rerun on Globo's "Sessão da Tarde," and Mario Jorge is Brazil's iconic dubbing voice for Eddie Murphy — around a central creative insight: "Eddie Murphys Brasileiros." The concept and its two locked executions, an AV piece ("Eddies in Brazil") and a merchandising tie-in with Rede Bandeirantes, were developed through a joint Netflix Brazil/Netflix US collaboration the team flagged internally as unprecedented. The retrospective noted a late-stage brief change and a tight one-day turnaround on the global deck, but ultimately positive organic engagement and PR pickup. The hero AV drew 1.5 million views with a 1.45% engagement rate, on a campaign that ran from March to July 2024.

title: HBO — Cidade de Deus S2 Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Reframing Cidade de Deus survivors as operators
longDescription: MATTER ran the full creative pipeline for HBO Max Brasil's Cidade de Deus Season 2 launch — from brief intake through unbranded cultural research, branded property and cast research, to a locked creative brief. Three independent research tracks converged on one platform: lead with a female operator aesthetic — composed, institutional, sophisticated — that only the series form can carry, as a contrast to the 2002 film's handheld urgency. Berenice, Jerusa and Leka are repositioned as operators, not survivors. The locked platform line is "Um lugar onde a justiça não chega estará sempre em disputa," tied to a broader cultural theme MATTER called "The Refusal of Resolution." Production covers key art, a teaser, and a trailer, running through multiple client review rounds; as of mid-July 2026 delivery was tracking toward mid-August, ahead of the series' November 8, 2026 launch.

title: Spotify — VidCon 2025
onePhraser: Pre-roll sizzle reel for Spotify at VidCon 2025
longDescription: A pre-recorded sizzle reel played on stage ahead of every live podcast-creator taping at VidCon 2025, built to reinforce Spotify as owner of the video-podcast category among Gen-Z audiences. The edit dives from a static podcast cover into video, then cuts through creator intros (Dropouts, No Filter with Zac Peter, The Unplanned Podcast, Sad Boyz, The Comment Section) and stat supers ("380,000+ video podcasts," "270 million+ viewers") before landing on the "Watch on Spotify" CTA. MATTER pitched a dynamic, expressive, human, bold visual style, using color and texture as storytelling tools, scored to a needle-drop for momentum, and built from previously approved clips from shows like The Louis Theroux Podcast, Two Hot Takes and Good Hang.

title: Spotify — Chicken Shop Date
onePhraser: Launch identity & social campaign for Chicken Shop Date
longDescription: Show-specific launch creative for the Chicken Shop Date podcast on Spotify, built across Penn Plaza, The Reef, TEC Tower and Underground 48 OOH placements plus a paid social campaign. Three rounds refined an earlier visual reference into a cleaner, image-forward layout: reducing the host's name treatment so photography could carry the ad, removing the border, smoothing the gradient, and keeping the white CTA legible against the background. The final round locked colors, capitalization and background treatment across the OOH options.

title: Motorola — Razr Swarovski
onePhraser: Limited-edition Razr made with Swarovski crystals
longDescription: Global launch of the Razr made with Swarovski crystals, explicitly briefed as a lifestyle and perception play rather than a sales or feature-led effort — a true limited edition with a lower volume forecast than other Razr devices. A key positioning constraint shaped the whole campaign: this is "Motorola made with Swarovski crystals," not a "Motorola x Swarovski" co-brand, which limited how much the Swarovski name and assets could be used. MATTER's answer was a 360° social-first effort extending the "No Apologies" territory from Razr Batches 1-2, leaning on creators, fashion-adjacent culture, and ambassador talent rather than a hero-asset-only rollout. The final cut, delivered May 20, 2025, opens on close-up shots of the Oboe earbuds x Swarovski partnership that preceded this launch, then balances lifestyle and studio settings 50/50. The campaign connects to the later Constellation work, which also combined Swarovski, Pantone and Bose.

title: Motorola — 2025 Edge
onePhraser: Edge's 'What's Your Edge?' durability-meets-passion films
longDescription: Second batch of 15-second films for the Edge franchise, made under Motorola's 2025 Global Brand Campaign Sprint Scope, which positioned Edge as the "Creative Legends" tier of the brand pyramid for makers with niche, eccentric passions. The creative question was "What's Your Edge?" — each spot pairs a visually striking passion (collecting, flower styling, gardening) with a character whose creativity is amplified, not interrupted, by a dramatic moment that proves the phone's durability. The standout is the Gardener spot: a fashion-forward gardener clipping a topiary gets soaked by a hidden hose, the phone survives, and the spot closes on "Unstoppable creativity" while quietly demonstrating Gorilla Glass 7i and IP68/IP69 water resistance without naming a single spec. Gardening looked like a risky pick for a youth audience until research showed it trending as a movement on TikTok and Instagram, which validated the call. Production rolled out in 2025 under agency stewardship.

title: St Ives — Brand Proposition Refresh
onePhraser: St. Ives bets on 'sensorial credibility' over clinical
longDescription: MATTER led Phase 1 strategy and creative direction for St. Ives' brand-proposition refresh, mapping the positioning territory between generic "easy wellness" and over-claimed clinical skincare for the brand's parent, Evermark. The locked bet is "sensorial credibility" — rich, textural, unmistakably physical — aimed at what the team called the "glow-seeking skinimalist": a woman 25–50 who has opted out of 12-step routines, self-educates on ingredients, and wants products that feel good to use, not just perform well on paper. The positioning wedge treats pleasure and efficacy as a single promise rather than a tradeoff, and rebuilds the apricot scrub — long treated as a liability — back into an asset: an exfoliant that feels like one. Work included a qualitative exploratory positioning study, a 4Cs category decomposition, an alignment deck, stimulus materials for consumer testing, and a strategy-lock deck delivered in Q1 2026. Consumer quantitative testing confirmed the positioning resonated, and the engagement closed with full alignment, handing off directly into the Brand Relaunch 2027 production project.

title: Alchemia - Reposicionamento de Marca
onePhraser: Full brand repositioning proposal for Alchemia
longDescription: MATTER submitted a full brand repositioning proposal to Alchemia, a beauty brand connected to Renner, in July 2026, valued at roughly USD 281,730 / BRL 1,464,998. The engagement is scoped to run through MATTER's seven-phase Brand Studio process — intake, 4Cs research across category, culture, consumer and company, positioning and purpose, brand operating system, verbal identity, a text-only design brief, and a final toolkit. As of the proposal date the deal is still in the Pipeline stage, awaiting a client decision, and no creative direction has been developed yet.

title: Elida Brands PDP Asset Creation
onePhraser: AI-augmented PDP system pitched to Elida Beauty
longDescription: MATTER pitched Elida Beauty (part of Evermark) a proposal called "PDP Intelligent Studio" — a production system for Amazon product pages covering 5 SKUs, with pack shots, 6–8 above-the-fold carousel assets, basic A+ Content, and at least one 15-second video per SKU, plus a PDP strategy document and EN/FR transcreation for Canada. The pitch leans on MATTER's existing Suave and ChapStick PDP production for Evermark as proof of concept, and proposes a routing engine that decides per asset whether photography or AI-generated imagery is the right production path, feeding a tagged, versioned asset library that gets cheaper with every additional SKU bundle. As of late July 2026 the proposal was restructured to a 2-week delivery timeline with pricing reframed around total value and asset-management economies of scale if the relationship expands to more Evermark brands. The deal remains in the Pipeline stage, awaiting client decision.

title: Goovi — Amazon Launch (US)
onePhraser: Goovi's Italian joy translated for Amazon US
longDescription: Goovi's first entry into the US market is an Amazon-first, PDP-led launch: 21 product pages across Supplements, Skin Care and Body Care, plus up to 210 landing-page tiles, display banners, videos, Sponsored Brands creative and a Brand Store. MATTER's core strategic move was to flip the brand's Italian order of operations: in Italy, personality (fronted by Michelle Hunziker) opens the door and proof earns the repeat; on Amazon, proof has to open the door and personality earns the repeat, so both must land on the same PDP, same scroll. The locked platform, "Your Feel-Good Obsession," stakes out joy as a functional claim rather than a tonal one — vibrant without superficial, natural without sanctimonious. The narrative was revised post-round-one to lean less clinical, reframing proof from clinical language to tangible, sensorial outcomes. As of late July 2026, PDP creative and copy are locked and in production, ahead of the August 13 delivery.

title: Q-tips Face Towels Launch
onePhraser: Cotton authority beats viscose with a towel joke
longDescription: Q-tips set out to win bottom-of-funnel conquest from Clean Skin Club — the eucalyptus-viscose brand that invented the "face towel" category — by reframing Q-tips from a cotton tool into a cotton beauty essential, using face-drying-as-skincare-step as the vehicle, not the goal. MATTER positioned Q-tips as a challenger with authority: new to the category, backed by 103 years of cotton specialization and the \#1 cotton brand claim, against a four-year-old, non-cotton upstart. The original brief centered a "dirty old towel" fear insight; MATTER pressure-tested it into humor instead — the gym towel becomes a light-hearted joke against which cotton is judged the standard. Deliverables totaled 11 hero concepts across paid social (Awareness, Consideration, Conversion, each in multiple aspect ratios) and retail display for Amazon and Walmart, plus a hero video and image bank. Originally due June 30, 2026, the work was renegotiated and delivered July 10, 2026, with the client approving the final film and all assets.

title: St Ives — Brand Relaunch 2027
onePhraser: St. Ives' 2027 relaunch, paused mid-production
longDescription: Building directly on the Brand Proposition Refresh's locked "sensorial credibility" positioning, this project translates that strategy into a full creative system for St. Ives' 2027 brand relaunch: a visual language of "glow and grit" — lived-in, renewed skin and tactile texture shots — under the line "light as the language of glow," rendered through dappled, refracted gradients, with a voice built as light-and-leveled, playfully-punchy and smoothly self-assured. The Apricot Scrub is rebuilt again as a hero asset: an exfoliant that feels like one. MATTER delivered a working deck and a full creative-rollout package, including external testing materials, but production paused when Evermark went through a post-merger reorganization (the Elida Beauty–Evermark merger). As of mid-2026 the project remains on hold, with a realistic resume in Q3 2026 at the earliest and the 2027 relaunch target intact.

title: Donos do Jogo S02
onePhraser: Season 2 in early development, teaser ideas underway
longDescription: Donos do Jogo S02 is still in early discovery/pipeline phase — the brief, creative approach, and results sections have not yet been filled in on record. The concrete activity so far: a director shortlist deck is being evaluated for the season, and the team has begun teaser ideation, sharing an initial concept document with Netflix for review in late July.

title: S&X — Creative Development
onePhraser: Cancelled Netflix key art development project
longDescription: S\&X was a Netflix key art development project that MATTER carried through a full six-round creative process, reaching creative lock and a full key art suite delivery in June 2026, with leadership added as co-lead partway through to raise creative ambition. The brief on record is thin beyond scope notes for "key art and timeline development," and the project's Slack channel was archived following delivery. Despite reaching delivery, project status is marked Cancelled, so no results or outcomes are documented.

title: Avatar S02 — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Earth-sculpted OOH brings the Earth Kingdom to Bahia
longDescription: Avatar: The Last Airbender is the live-action series built on the four elements: fire, water, earth, and air. Season 2 is 100% focused on earth, so instead of advertising it, we made earth the medium: a billboard built entirely from soil, shaped by hand by a Brazilian artisan. The idea started with Toph: the world's greatest earthbender wouldn't run an ad. She'd turn one into earth. That premise shaped a format built from the ground up: a physical version of the Earth Kingdom instead of a conventional media placement. The billboard took 90 hours of handmade work, using 120 kg of earth to build a structure 2.2 meters tall, with no machinery and no digital enhancement. It stood in Feira de Santana, a Brazilian city fans nicknamed the "Brazilian Ba Sing Se" for its resemblance to the Earth Kingdom's capital, a fan-service layer without being the campaign's premise. The campaign demonstrated how listening to fans can create stronger cultural connections than inventing a new narrative. By recognizing and legitimizing an existing community conversation, Netflix reinforced its fan-service approach and turned a long-running online reference into a real-world experience. Once live, it reached nearly 6 million views and drove more than 58,000 engagements across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Facebook. The story didn't stay online: news outlets, sites and portals covered it organically, turning a handmade idea into headlines.

title: Enola Holmes 3 — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: WAGs "reveal" they were watching Enola, not the Cup
longDescription: To launch Enola Holmes 3 during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, when Brazilians' attention was on football, Netflix went after the WAG of the Brazilian team's most beloved player. Gabriely Miranda had gone viral years earlier for writing a relationship contract with Endrick while they were still dating, full of controversial clauses on what he could and couldn't say or do. Enola Holmes 3 opens with one question: will Enola say yes to the wedding. Gabriely already had an answer. She argued Enola wouldn't be crazy enough to marry without a contract, so she wrote one herself: a full marriage contract for Enola Holmes. With the World Cup taking over every feed, partnering with the WAG of the tournament's most talked-about player gave the film a natural way into a conversation Netflix couldn't otherwise interrupt, turning a familiar joke into a bridge to the story. The campaign reached nearly 7.9 million views and drove more than 144,000 engagements across Instagram, X, Threads, TikTok and Facebook. Endrick himself commented on the post and shared it organically on his Instagram Stories, without any commercial partnership, and the story spread further still, picked up organically by entertainment and gossip news sites.

title: Kian's Bizarre B&B — Season 2
onePhraser: Kian84 hosts a chaotic winter B\&B with K-pop stars
longDescription: Season two of Kian's Bizarre B\&B relocates webtoon artist and TV personality Kian84's guesthouse to Daegwallyeong, a snowbound 33,000m² stretch of Korean mountain at roughly 1,000m elevation. Joining him as staff are volleyball legend Kim Yeon-koung, actor-singer Lee Junho (2PM) and LE SSERAFIM's Kazuha, running chores and mishaps for the cameras. The creative brief centers on a "bab-chingu" (meal buddy) idea — easy, stress-free comfort viewing built for single-person households — and a deliberate choice to withhold the guesthouse's true scale from pre-launch key art, letting audiences discover it once the show airs. Key art direction leans colorful, casual and raw rather than cinematic or Nordic-minimalist, framing the cast front and center in heavy winter gear against windmills and snow-covered ridges, doing dynamic chores rather than posing. As of writing, the project is in creative development, working through key art rounds ahead of a September 22, 2026 launch.

title: Marcha das Onças — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: True fable of matriarch jaguars guarding the Pantanal
longDescription: Marcha das Onças is a Brazilian Netflix documentary film following a lineage of female jaguars who guard the Meeting of the Waters in the Pantanal, narrated by Fernanda Torres and directed by Lawrence Wahba and Mike Bueno — the team behind March of the Penguins. The story follows matriarch Patrícia guiding Marcela and Rio through a true story of survival, courage and legacy. Positioning steers deliberately toward prestige and pride in a proudly Brazilian production, and away from any "violent animals vs. humans" framing; the trailer arc opens by subverting the assumption that jaguars are simply savage, then builds emotional family drama toward an epic close. Key art went through several client rounds, including a director-preferred fusion of two design options and fixes to make producer and talent credentials (Oscar-winning producers, Fernanda Torres's Golden Globe, Lawrence Wahba's Emmy) legible. The campaign targets documentary and nature fans as its core, with family co-viewing as an opportunity audience, ahead of an October 22, 2026 launch.

title: Mission: Cross 2 — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Power-couple spies race to recover stolen treasures
longDescription: Mission: Cross 2 is the sequel to the Korean action-comedy hit Mission: Cross, reuniting ex-special-ops agent Kang-mu (Hwang Jung-min) and detective wife Mi-seon (Yum Jung-ah) as a now battle-hardened team recruited by the President to recover stolen national treasures. Where the first film's hook was role-reversal (tough detective wife, house-husband ex-agent), the sequel evolves the couple into a unified, in-sync duo, with scale expanded to an ensemble including a tomb-raiding fence in iron armor and a presidential-bodyguard-turned-conspirator. Key art hierarchy keeps the couple inseparable and face-visible, layers in franchise-signature crosshair/scope motifs and Korean heritage landmarks, and is directed firmly toward commercial action-comedy rather than an Indiana Jones-style treasure hunt or an overtly patriotic tone. The film releases September 23, 2026; the project was in creative development, including debate over how far to push AI-assisted retouching on key art featuring real talent.

title: Nando Entre Dois Mundos — Creative Development
onePhraser: Creative development for the Sintonia spin-off series
longDescription: Nando Entre Dois Mundos is a spin-off of the hit Brazilian series Sintonia, and this project covered its creative development phase — positioning, key art and title treatment leading to a client-approved key art and full finishing pipeline. Netflix approved framing the marketing language around "um filme Sintonia" rather than "um filme Netflix," underscoring the project's franchise continuity. Creative rounds ran through to final approval and creative lock in early May 2026, followed by a three-round finishing process closing out in June 2026 ahead of delivery. Detail beyond this operational record is thin — the brief itself is logged only as creative development for the Sintonia spin-off, with most substance coming from meeting notes and milestone tracking rather than a fleshed-out creative brief.

title: Os 12 Signos de Valentina — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Astrology-as-language rom-com key art system
longDescription: Os 12 Signos de Valentina is a Brazilian rom-com series (8 x 30min, Q4 2026) from Boutique Filmes starring Giovanna Grigio as Valentina, who — after a breakup blamed on "astrological incompatibility" — sets out to date one man from every zodiac sign and chronicle it on a videocast, only to fall for a guy with no sign at all. The key art challenge treats astrology not as mysticism but as the social shorthand young Brazilian women already use to name feelings and roast their exes, landing a modern, culturally specific rom-com tone that reads young-adult rather than teen. The brief explicitly warns against a magazine-cover aesthetic and against repeating the sofa-pose composition of Grigio's recent film poster. Multiple key art territories were explored in parallel — a street-flyer graphic language, a duplicated social-native composition, a mystical zodiac-wheel treatment, a classic bouquet, and pattern-driven zodiac symbology — all keeping Grigio central. The project is flagged internally as a flagship account, with key art reaching creative lock as it heads toward a Q4 2026 launch measured on conversation rather than pure awareness.

title: Take a Hike! — Launch Campaign (Netflix Korea)
onePhraser: Celebrities forced up Korea's snow peaks, reluctantly
longDescription: Take a Hike\! (하산악회) is Netflix Korea's first hiking reality show: four celebrity hiking novices — ALLDAY PROJECT's TARZZAN, singer-songwriter Cha Jung-won, DAY6 drummer Dowoon, and actor Lee Chae-min — form a mock "hiking club" and are thrown into winter ascents of Mt. Seorak, Mt. Taebaek, Mt. Halla, the Yeongnam Alps and Jirisan across 10 episodes. The key art brief is built around the show's own central question, "why on earth do people go hiking?", with the audience meant to watch four reluctant city-dwellers freeze, bicker and slowly find the answer. Creative direction called for a feel-good, Gen Z-tuned tone, rolled out across three escalating stages: a Tease emphasizing scale and silhouette, a Main stage foregrounding chemistry and humor, and a Launch stage combining winter intensity, friendship and iconic Korean peaks. The project reached full suite approval in July 2026, and launches August 18, 2026.

title: Take Charge of My Heart (나를 충전해줘)
onePhraser: Rom-com about a fading heart and an electric woman
longDescription: Take Charge of My Heart (나를 충전해줘) is a 10-episode Korean rom-com in which a man with a failing artificial heart battery (Kim Young-kwang) strikes a deal with a woman who carries literal electricity in her body (Chae Soo-bin) to keep him alive — and the two end up charging each other's hearts instead. Netflix Korea's first-round key art feedback was pointed: the colors read too intense, the electric effects looked more sci-fi than K-romcom, and the lead's signature frizzy "static hair" effect was missing entirely. Revisions pushed toward a softer palette, lightning confined subtly to the hands, a more prominent pink rubber glove as a character prop, and backgrounds that read as original rather than direct homages to reference images. Constraints throughout included a strict no-real-talent-faces-on-AI-generated-art rule. The project moved through multiple rounds into product-suite retouching and client review, targeting an October 9, 2026 launch.

title: Dom de Iludir — Creative Development
onePhraser: Melodrama tagline: the only truth is the lies
longDescription: Creative development — positioning, key art, title treatment, and teaser AV — for Dom de Iludir, a 10-episode melodrama/thriller about a wealthy Rio family whose inheritance battle draws in a family of grifters. The locked tagline, "A Única Verdade São As Mentiras" ("The Only Truth Is Lies"), was built around a rule that every character lies for a different reason — to protect, to seduce, to profit, to escape. Key art direction used the sun as a recurring emotional device, comforting or oppressive depending on the character, set against the family's art-world backdrop. Title treatment went through several rounds chasing an elegant, "novelesque" serif feel, including an inverted R as a visual nod to illusion and confusion. Shooting happened in April 2026; the project cycled on and off hold through mid-2026 en route to a planned December 2026 launch, with the shoot's key art since moved into horizontal deployment per client feedback.

title: Rauls — Creative Dev + Production
onePhraser: Digital-scam gang thriller from São Paulo's periferia
longDescription: Rauls is a Brazilian drama-thriller series about a young man from São Paulo's periferia who rises to lead a digital-scam gang chasing economic ascension and social visibility — created, directed and led by talent from that same community. The creative platform leans into "visual dopamine": golpes digitais, ostentação, dinheiro and ambição as pillars, positioned as nuanced fiction rather than a realistic, glamorizing portrait of crime. The locked concept plays on Brazil's fraud statute (article 171) — a 7 disguised inside the title treatment's L, and a registered-trademark symbol that becomes a smile when a scam succeeds — alongside two key art directions: a top-down "table" of colorful objects from a scammer's daily life, and a high-contrast, flash-lit "gang" portrait of the cast. The hero AV script follows lead character Biel calmly running a fake bank-verification call while the camera pulls back to reveal the mansion and party his scam funds. MATTER led creative development through lock in January 2026 and AV production for a Telemarketing spot, targeting a December 16, 2026 launch.

title: Bad Boas — Product Creative
onePhraser: Rebranding Bon Bini into Hollywood-quality key art
longDescription: Product creative (key art and PDP art) for Bad Boa's (English title: Almost Cops), a Rotterdam-set buddy-cop comedy about a community service officer and a reckless ex-detective who discover they share the loss of a murdered loved one. The brief explicitly framed the work as "an exercise in rebranding" — moving the title's visual identity from its "Bon Bini" roots to Hollywood-quality creative: warm, saturated, talent-forward, with lead Ramon required in every piece of art. Delivered 3–6 unique billboard artworks plus the full derivative suite (billboard, story panel, boxshot, title card) across three creative rounds for a July 2025 launch.

title: Congonhas: Tragédia Anunciada — Product Creative
onePhraser: Key art built from wreckage, not victims
longDescription: Product creative strategy for Season 1 of this documentary series retelling Brazil's deadliest air disaster, the 2007 Congonhas crash. The brief deliberately kept people out of the artwork — no recognizable faces, no black box, no plane mid-flight — building the visual language instead from the crash site, the airport, air-traffic-control radar screens, and the aircraft's wreckage. Concepts explored an eyewitness point-of-view of the crash, a close-up on the failed landing attempt in heavy rain, and a composition built around the pilots' throttle-lever error that destabilized the plane. Round 2 feedback pushed the team toward a more realistic (less sketch-like) treatment after early images were mistaken by international colleagues for a terrorist attack rather than an accident. The title launched April 30, 2025.

title: Familia Pero No Mucho — Product Creative
onePhraser: Key art and title treatment across five rounds
longDescription: Product creative development — key art and title treatment — for Família Pero No Mucho, developed with agency Boys Do Cry across five creative rounds. Title treatment exploration tested two typographic options in 60/40, dark, and light color variants before locking a final direction, carried through to the full set of derivative assets across Netflix touchpoints: billboard, display art, story art, and title card. Delivered October 2025.

title: How to Ruin Love S2 — Creative Development
onePhraser: Cows, chaos, and two families feuding over lobola
longDescription: Creative development for How to Ruin Love: The Lobola Season 2, the romantic-comedy spinoff of the How to Ruin Christmas franchise, following the Phatudi and Dzana families clashing over lobola negotiations ahead of a Western-style wedding. Four creative directions were explored: "Comedy of Errors," playing up escalating misunderstandings; "Worlds Apart," using split-screen to contrast the two families; "Love Love Love," centered on the couple's romance; and "Cows, the Actual Lobola," pairing live cattle with the cast to visualize the literal tradition. The brief specifically called for treating lobola respectfully — framed as honoring a new family rather than ownership — and for portraying the village setting in a positive light. Season 2 launched December 19, 2025, with six final artworks plus the full derivative asset suite delivered across three creative rounds.

title: WLGYT — Marketing Campaign
onePhraser: Alcione sings a K-drama theme song in Korean
longDescription: The marketing campaign for When Life Gives You Tangerines (WLGYT) in Brazil was built on two discoveries: that 75% of Netflix Brazil members watch Korean content, and that the geography and culture of São Luís, Maranhão has real parallels with Korea's Jeju Island, where the K-drama is set. The creative idea cast São Luís's own iconic singer Alcione as the campaign's centerpiece, having her perform the show's theme song in Korean for a hero AV and photo activation — a culturally improbable pairing that leaned on an existing, organic fan community in São Luís that already held independent meetups. The rollout paired the Alcione AV with a fan screening event and a marquee display in São Luís. Production partners delivered the song and film inside a two-week window. The retrospective flagged scheduling friction on shoot day but rated the idea a strong success — the project is flagged as case-study-ready and awards-worthy.

title: Avatar S01 — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Avatar live-action launch featuring Leo Santana
longDescription: Launch campaign for Netflix's live-action Avatar: The Last Airbender, adapting the global campaign deck for the Brazilian market. The core challenge was winning over a skeptical, vocal anime fanbase while still pulling in new viewers unfamiliar with the animated original. Creative went through multiple rounds, with Round 3 bringing in Brazilian singer Leo Santana for a talent activation tied to the show. Measured results were modest: a "Reels Trio" post generated 448,467 engagements, and a tweet featuring Aang drew 629,500 views and 3,595 engagements (0.57% engagement rate).

title: Candelaria — KAs + Positioning
onePhraser: Candelária Massacre drama repositioned as prestige TV
longDescription: Key art, positioning, opening titles, and title treatment for Candelária, a limited series dramatizing the 1993 Candelária Massacre of street children in Rio de Janeiro. The original brief positioned the show as a provocative must-see drama built on the insight that "all kids should have the right to live and to dream." In April 2024 the project was given a full repositioning: a new main key art built around a first-person monologue voiced from the perspective of the murdered children ("A gente passa fome todo dia..."), and several rounds of title-treatment work pushing toward a more "prestige" typographic feel after early options were flagged as "pouco sofisticado." A dedicated trailer was also scoped in May 2024. The project went on hold before any campaign metrics were published.

title: Fuga das Galinhas 2 — Launch Campaign
onePhraser: Bruna Griphão AV plus a Globo Sessão da Tarde takeover
longDescription: Launch campaign for Fuga das Galinhas 2 (Chicken Run: Dawn of the Nugget) in Brazil, combining stunt ideation with AV production. The centerpiece was a film starring Bruna Griphão, paired with a set of bespoke scripts written to run inside Globo's "Sessão da Tarde" broadcast block — including a bit where TUDUM interrupts the Globo signal, a meta joke about Netflix paying for the placement, and a K-drama parody. A separate concept embedded one-second subliminal flashes of Griphão's face into the trailer. Results: the Bruna Griphão AV reached 14.8M views and 293,163 engagements (1.98% engagement rate); the Globo spots aired on-air during Sessão da Tarde. A planned balloon-parade-style stunt was cut for timeline reasons, and the Globo bespoke edit needed six revision rounds against a standard three.

title: Spotify — Podfluence
onePhraser: Spotify Podfluence — creative bundle pending
longDescription: A Spotify social project centered on podcast creator/influencer amplification ("Podfluence"), with the external delivery timeline locked but the full creative bundle not yet loaded into the archive. No brief detail, creative approach or outcome documentation is available on this page yet.

title: Spotify — Audiobooks Always On 2026
onePhraser: Always-on OOH campaign for Spotify Audiobooks catalog
longDescription: Continuation of Spotify's audiobooks growth work, running OOH placements at Penn Plaza and The Reef across February, March and May 2026 flight packs, plus multiple rounds of creative briefs. The always-on campaign targets listeners not yet using Spotify for audiobooks, aiming to build catalog awareness and frame audiobooks as a natural extension of everyday listening on the platform. The SOW was fully executed; performance figures live in Spotify's internal reporting rather than this brief.

title: Spotify — Audiobooks H1 2026 Performance Media
onePhraser: Paid social & search ads driving Audiobooks+ conversions
longDescription: H1 2026 performance media push for Audiobooks+, Spotify's recurring audiobook add-on live in 19 markets. MATTER built paid social and search creative (Meta, TikTok, Snap) for en-US, with Spotify handling localization for CA, GB, SE, FI and DK, targeting Premium subscribers who already listen to audiobooks elsewhere but not on Spotify. Creative tested title-led, price-led and "all in one place" messaging, built to flex between trial and non-trial pricing since SE/FI/DK launched with a 3-month free trial in February while US/CA/GB stayed trial-free until April. The brief called for creative that felt "visually Spotify" and music-inspired; asset delivery and localization were locked to a February 2 campaign flight start running through June 30.

title: Spotify — Audiobooks LATFOB 2026 Stage Video
onePhraser: Author-driven stage video for LATFOB 2026 book fest
longDescription: A pre-recorded stage video for Spotify's presence at the LA Times Festival of Books, playing ahead of every panel on the "Audiobook and Podcast Stage Presented by Spotify" (April 18-19, 2026). Built from pre-approved author footage (Mark Ronson, Dua Lipa, Tina Knowles, Jordan Chiles, Bruce Holsinger, Rachel Reid, Harlan Coben and others) plus new features Page Match and Physical Books via Bookshop.org, the spot tells a "from audiobooks to all books" story. The script went through several rewrites — an emotional brand-spot direction, then a stripped-down alternative — landing on a 60-second sizzle reel with the Premium subscriber-catalog legal disclaimer built in.

title: Spotify — Audiobooks VIP 2.0
onePhraser: Multi-batch OOH & CTV push for Audiobooks awareness
longDescription: Second wave ("VIP 2.0") of Spotify Audiobooks awareness creative, spanning CTV, paid social and OOH (Penn Plaza, The Reef, JFK) across multiple production batches and a later "new exploration" round. Work included TikTok safe-zone corrections, home banner brightness fixes, logo/title layout variants for "Best Books of the Century/Year," and paid social copy for specific titles built around the CTA "Audiobooks. Included in Premium." As of the June 2026 status check the project remained active in the Creative phase, moving through sequential production and new-request rounds.

title: Spotify — Podcasts Always On 2026
onePhraser: Monthly OOH billboards for Spotify's podcast slate
longDescription: 2026 continuation of Spotify's always-on podcast retainer, producing monthly Penn Plaza and Reef billboard creative for the paid-social and OOH push. The March 2026 pack alone covered five shows — Dissect, Hot Smart Rich, Killer Stories, Friends Keep Secrets and Equal Podcast — each getting its own Penn Plaza motion unit and three-sided Reef static execution, iterated across several layout options before mockup lock. The retainer follows the same monthly cadence as the 2025 always-on program, swapping in new title billboards as Spotify's slate changes month to month.

title: Spotify — Good Hang
onePhraser: OOH & social launch for Amy Poehler's Good Hang
longDescription: Launch creative for Good Hang, Amy Poehler's video podcast on Spotify, split into separate OOH and social workstreams by round three. The brief leaned entirely on Amy as the hero, using the show's own tagline logic — "No advice. No better you. Just Amy having fun. Watch on Spotify" — for a two-panel animated Penn Plaza unit, plus a three-panel static Reef execution repeating the message across all three faces so it lands regardless of which side a viewer sees. On social, three 15-second vertical films spotlighted Amy's goofy, self-deprecating energy and her own descriptions of the show, each cut with and without text supers.

title: Spotify — Podcasts Always On 2025
onePhraser: Monthly always-on social & OOH for Spotify podcasts
longDescription: Year-long always-on retainer producing monthly paid-social AV assets and OOH creative for Spotify's Original & Licensed podcast slate through 2025, plus a Golden Globes activation and a January 2026 OOH pack that closed out the retainer. Each month spotlighted 2-3 "Podcasts of the Month" (Anything Goes, Two Hot Takes, The Rest Is Football, Service95 Book Club with Dua Lipa, Diary of a CEO, The Louis Theroux Podcast) as 15-second video cutdowns, built round by round: scene selection first, then motion, visual ID, subtitles, profanity/IP review, captions and safe zones. The Golden Globes activation extended the same OOH toolkit to call out nominees and winners across shows like Call Her Daddy, Smartless and Good Hang.

title: Spotify — Podcasts Branding O&L Bumpers
onePhraser: Animated "A Spotify Podcast" bumper for video pods
longDescription: A universal video bumper attributing Original & Licensed podcasts to Spotify, since the "A Spotify Podcast" credit gets lost on platforms like YouTube and disappears once clips move to social. Inspired by an earlier bumper from the Podfluencer Toolkit, the team locked a direction built around an animated speech-bubble motif conveying conversation, working in alpha so it drops into any episode's cold open. Five rounds refined the motion, added a bright-green color swap and dark/light variants for readability, and produced matching vertical and horizontal cuts with in/out transitions. The card runs in an episode's opening seconds with the intro sting ducked slightly underneath. Brief kicked off August 21, 2025; launched September 4, 2025.

title: Spotify — Two Hot Takes
onePhraser: Launch creative for Spotify's Two Hot Takes video pod
longDescription: Launch campaign introducing Two Hot Takes as a video podcast on Spotify, aimed at Gen-Z and millennial women, positioning the show as "the next must-watch podcast." Fifteen-second social cutdowns adapted viral Reddit-story episode clips into TikTok- and YouTube-native captions, run alongside a two-panel animated Penn Plaza unit and three-panel static Reef unit in NY and LA. Three feedback rounds moved the visual identity from the show's original neon logo options into full alignment with Spotify's brand guidelines — Spotify Mix typeface, brand palette, "Watch on Spotify" CTA — while narrative testing settled on the host reading the story live with the guest reacting. A set of unused "spicy" activation ideas was also banked for future rounds.

title: NewCo — Brand Launch 2026
onePhraser: A 'modern legacy' brand for AI-native finance
longDescription: NewCo (working name, brand name "Norai Society") is an AI-native strategic finance and advisory firm launching in Barcelona through a partnership with Gutiérrez Pujadas Asociados, serving Catalan SMEs in the €2M–€8M revenue range with a three-layer service model, targeting €9.3M revenue and 32% EBITDA margin by year four. MATTER ran the full seven-phase Brand Studio process for the launch, positioning the firm explicitly as a strategic finance partner — not an asesoría, not a fractional CFO shop, not an AI company. The founder held an early aesthetic hypothesis that the brand should feel like a "modern legacy" institution, borrowing restraint and world-building from consumer references like J.Crew, Sporty & Rich, The Row and Soho House, and Phase 2 research tested whether that consumer-luxury frame could earn trust in Spanish B2B professional-services finance. The engagement passed its positioning-and-purpose gate and ran through verbal identity, a text-only design brief, and a final toolkit, closing out complete under the Norai Society name, including a manifesto, origin story and brand boilerplate.

title: Kunumi — Retainer Contínuo (Jul/26–Jan/27)
onePhraser: Kunumi's ongoing editorial and cultural retainer
longDescription: Following the ICLR 2026 event, MATTER won a continuous retainer with Instituto Kunumi (confirmed July 3, 2026) covering three tracks: a Matter Session (up to four leadership conversations as pre-work), an Editorial & Cultural Platform running August 2026 through January 2027 with two content pieces a month, a "Levitation" activation, and two proprietary events (a Colabs event and Kunumi's 10th-anniversary event, moved to sit near Levitation), plus institutional campaign extensions including one deliverable tied to the BRACIS conference in October. Total investment is R$580,000 across six monthly installments. As of late July 2026 the contract is awaiting formal signature, a visual-references concept deck for the Colabs event is being presented to the client, and Kunumi has raised an additional ask for production support on a press conference tied to the Levitation festival launch.

title: ICLR 2026 — OOH + Event Experience
onePhraser: An AI institute's no-screens conference presence
longDescription: For ICLR 2026, one of the world's largest AI research conferences, Instituto Kunumi asked for a presence that had nothing to do with showcasing AI in the conventional sense: no screens, no keynote, no speech, no branding exercise. MATTER delivered a bilingual OOH campaign across Rio de Janeiro (including Santos Dumont airport) built around the question "Where am I in AI?", paired with an evening experience at Sítio Roberto Burle Marx on April 25, 2026 — curated music, handmade food, no agenda, just conversation, with an hourglass and bilingual letter as the parting gift for each guest. Kunumi is an AI research institute with roughly 20 partner labs and ties to Stanford, MIT and Harvard, framing science as awakening rather than accumulation. The event was described internally as "a blueprint for future initiatives" and secured strong buy-in from client leadership, directly leading to the follow-on Kunumi retainer.

title: Motorola — Edge Franchise Playbook (FY26/27)
onePhraser: FY26/27 strategic playbook for the Edge franchise
longDescription: A year-long strategic and creative system for the Edge franchise, covering positioning, messaging architecture, creative guardrails, a 360° campaign framework and hero lifestyle-film direction across Edge's full price spread. The brief: define what "premium" means for Edge without claiming the ceiling that Signature and Razr occupy above it, while holding one coherent identity across the widest portfolio range in the Motorola lineup. Scope includes a Synthetic Consumer Lab research phase plus coordinated external-institute fieldwork, and excludes production. Awarded alongside the sibling Moto G playbook in the same RFP cycle, with a shared strategy lead running both engagements over roughly 17 working weeks. As of late July 2026, the creative platform has been decided — "Everything For Your Thing," anchored on personalization and framing Edge for premium moments that prioritize personal joy over daily utility — with strategy and creative work underway ahead of a November 2026 final delivery.

title: Motorola — Moto G Franchise Playbook (FY26/27)
onePhraser: FY26/27 franchise system for Moto G's volume line
longDescription: A year-long strategic and creative system for Moto G, Motorola's volume entry-point franchise, meant to make repeated launches throughout the year read as one consistent franchise instead of a rerun. Motorola came in with its own strategic groundwork already built — the essence "Style and tech, democratized," two candidate messaging platforms, and five key-selling-point pillars (battery, camera, style/durability, display/audio, performance) each with its own key-visual line. The production model behind it, "Capture Once. Build Many. Adapt Infinitely," uses one master gallery shoot covering all six pillars, with each new device launch highlighting two or three of them and reusing scenes with the device swapped via AI. MATTER's scope covers lifestyle creative direction only — CGI direction stays with Motorola's internal Creative Hub — plus positioning, messaging architecture, and the full playbook deliverable, running from July through an October 30, 2026 final delivery.

title: Motorola — Blue Harvest
onePhraser: Pantone Color of 2026 launch via Cloud Dancers film
longDescription: Motorola's tie-in to Pantone's Color of the Year 2026, built around the concept "The Lightness of Being" — an editorial exploration of weightlessness and fluid movement, anchored by a recurring visual motif called Cloud Dancers. Rather than slap the year's color on as a graphic overlay, the campaign treats it as an emotional register: lightness, freedom, drift, expressed through dance. Planning began in October 2025 against a hard embargo — no promotional material could run before December 4, 2025 — and that date shaped every downstream production and media decision. The partnership positions Motorola as the device-side launch partner for one of the highest-profile annual moments in design and fashion, reinforcing its lifestyle-tech credentials. Deliverables centered on a lifestyle hero film and key visual plus a supporting asset suite, rolling into production and launch through 2026.

title: Motorola — Constellation
onePhraser: Bose, Pantone, Swarovski unite in 'Edge of Light'
longDescription: A 45-second spot for Motorola Signature and the Moto Buds 2 Plus (Sound by Bose), built around a Pantone-licensed color and Swarovski's Urus and Bass Constellation crystals — completing a three-partner stack (Bose for sound, Pantone for color, Swarovski for crystal) that Motorola hadn't operationalized together before. The concept, "The Edge of Light," is set in the purple twilight zone between day and night, where light selectively reveals only the parts of a person that want to be seen — and when those pieces align, they form their own constellation. The tagline, "crafted for those who see beyond," avoids any feature callout in favor of a stance. The spot delivered across multiple aspect ratios for 2026 launch, with full brand, product and partner lockups, standing as a proof point for Motorola's premium lifestyle-tech positioning — three luxury-adjacent partnerships held together by one mood rather than a logo parade.

title: Motorola — Moto AI
onePhraser: Moto AI shown through three lifestyle-first stories
longDescription: A Q4 2025 series of three 15-second films — Date Name, Next Move, and Pottery — showing Moto AI as a quiet presence in everyday moments rather than a feature demo. Date Name shows AI helping in a relational moment, Next Move in a decision moment, and Pottery in a creative-hobby moment, echoing the same insight behind Edge's Gardener spot: tactile, physical creative practice reads as more honest on camera than productivity use cases. All three reinforce a human-first framing of AI that Motorola carried into Razr's Gemini-led "Flat Tire" spot and Moto Indigo's messaging about technology becoming personal. Internal kickoff ran November 25, 2025, with creative lock January 19, 2026, and delivery spanning Q4 2025 into Q1 2026 across standard global ratios.

title: Motorola — Moto Fifa
onePhraser: Motorola's 'Football Self' takes over for FIFA 2026
longDescription: Motorola's global campaign as Official Smartphone Partner of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, built around the insight that during the tournament "logic steps aside" and everyone's "Football Self takes over." The 60-second hero film, "Life Says," opens on Earth spinning in space, match-cuts into a football, and follows a fan's football-self taking over — with regional cutdowns split by language: "soccer is calling" for North America, "football is calling" everywhere else. Four messaging pillars tie the emotional story to product features: fan self-expression through device design, capturing and sharing moments, camera performance, and Moto AI. The campaign moved through a Global Campaign Briefing, Strategic Territories, and Production Brief creative lock, landing Motorola alongside past World Cup sponsors like Coca-Cola, Adidas and Hyundai. Delivered as a 60-second hero plus 30-second cutdowns for the 2026 tournament window.

title: Motorola — Moto Indigo
onePhraser: Launching Moto Indigo, Motorola's new signature color
longDescription: Launch of Moto Indigo, a Pantone-curated indigo blue introduced as Motorola's new global brand signature color, meant to connect indigo's cultural history to Motorola's design heritage and push the brand's perception from value-tech toward lifestyle-tech. Motorola's brief asked for a 30–60 second hero video plus five 15-second pills; MATTER expanded that into a single 83-second hero film tracing a Legacy-to-Present-to-Future arc, backed by four 15-second pillar cutdowns — Color As Identity, Color With Intention, Design & Lifestyle, and Empowerment — closing on the line "Moto Indigo. A point of view." Because Indigo is meant to be a permanent brand asset rather than a one-off campaign, delivery included a full open-file tool kit so future campaigns could rebuild from the originals. Production kicked off internally February 4, 2026, with client review February 9 and tool-kit delivery February 24 — a tight window that ran straight through Carnaval.

title: Motorola — Razr Batch 1-2
onePhraser: Razr's 'Make It Iconic' status-symbol film trilogy
longDescription: The first two batches of 2025 Razr campaign films, built on the idea "Make It Iconic" and shifting the brand conversation from "Razr was cool back in the day" to "Razr is an icon, and I am iconic with it." Three character-led stories each pair a Razr feature with an iconic-moment scene: a musician using tent mode in a music store, a museum-adjacent gallery sequence, and a roller skater navigating a subway station using the external display for music and closed-phone navigation. Each carries the "Make It Iconic" super and the hero device, the Razr 60 Ultra in Orion Rio Red. The work coincided with a genuine commercial shift — Razr's North American foldable market share rose from 30.1% in 2024 to 44.1% in 2025, closing the gap on Samsung's 50.9% — and this creative was the consumer-facing surface of that growth. Delivered across 30s/15s/6s cuts and the full ratio set.

title: Motorola — Razr Batch 3
onePhraser: Three feature-led Razr shorts: camera, durability, Gemini
longDescription: Three 15-second Razr films, each built around a single feature, continuing the "No Apologies" territory established in Batches 1-2 for a Gen Z and Millennial audience: Photo Booth Mode showcases gesture-activated group photos with a countdown timer and instant collage; Durability challenges the flip-phone fragility myth with a pavement drop and a puddle landing that leave the phone unmarked; and Gemini AI's "Flat Tire" spot shows a stranded couple using Razr's tent mode to watch YouTube while Gemini suggests next moves, refining its advice as they respond. During the revision process, the team cut the film's opening lipstick moment entirely to fit the AI story into 15 seconds, and changed the stranded driver's companion from a second woman to a man to avoid an unintended "women can't change tires" read. This batch also marked the point where decision authority for Razr formally passed from Motorola Global to Motorola North America.

title: Motorola — The Crew
onePhraser: Moto G's documentary-style 'Are You In?' crew stories
longDescription: ROW and NA campaign films for Moto G, built under the 2025 Global Brand Campaign Sprint Scope, which cast Moto G as "Trusted Essentials" — technology and style at an accessible price for a "Delightfully Defiant" audience. The concept, "The Crew," is a documentary-style world anchored to three reference cities by region — Rio, Tokyo, Madrid — with character profiles and dummy scripts guiding local production, under the tagline "Are You In?" Partway through development the team course-corrected against the work drifting into "skippable advertising," locking in two rules: relevance has to come from phones already integrated into characters' real lives, not demoed, and the differentiator is a plural, authentic sense of community rather than a manufactured one. A parallel NA track folded Stylus features into entertainment-style stories, including a Trip Journal spot demonstrating Moto Note's sketch-to-image photo-collage workflow. Delivery rolled out in 2025 under agency production stewardship.
